title: 第143章 夏深第142章 夏风
content_zh:
李子酱做好那天，青州城下了入夏以来的第一场暴雨。
雨是从下午开始下的，天一下子暗下来，像是有人把一张灰色的布盖在了城上面。风很大，把槐树的叶子吹得翻过来，露出背面浅白色的叶脉。方圆站在正房门口，看着雨落下来。雨点砸在青石板上，溅起白色的水花，很快就汇成了细流，顺着石板的缝隙往低处淌。王紫璇从厨房探出头来，“你站在那干什么？进来避雨。”方圆走回屋里，在门槛上坐下来。雨打在瓦片上，声音很密，像是有人在屋顶敲小鼓。
“李子酱做好了。”王紫璇把一个小陶罐放在桌上，“你尝尝。”方圆站起来，走到桌前，掀开盖子。酱是深红色的，亮晶晶的，散发着淡淡的甜香。他用手沾了一点，放进嘴里。甜的，带一点酸，回味很长。“好吃。”他说。王紫璇没有说话，嘴角微微弯了一下，像是在笑，又像是在确认什么。她把盖子盖好，放回桌上，“放着慢慢吃。”
雨一直在下，没有停的意思。院子里积了水，井台被淹了半截。那两棵树站在雨里，被风吹得东倒西歪，但根扎得很牢。方圆站在窗口看了一会儿，又走回去坐下。“树不会有事吧？”王紫璇也站在窗口看，“不会。它们已经扎根了。”她说这话的时候语气很平常，方圆没有接话，只是靠在椅背上，听着雨声，像是把整个夏天的热都等来了这场雨。
傍晚的时候，雨小了一些。方小石撑着一把伞跑来，站在门口，伞上的水滴滴答答地往下淌。“方圆哥，我娘让我来看看你。她说下这么大的雨，你院子里那两棵树会不会被冲倒？”“不会。根扎得深。”方小石探头看了看，确认树都还稳稳地站着，点了点头，“那我回去了。我娘还在等我回去吃饭。”他撑着伞跑走了，踩过水洼的时候溅起一片水花。
雨停了之后，院子里的空气变得很干净，青石板被冲洗得发亮，连墙角的青苔都绿了几分。方小石第二天来的时候，第一件事就是去看那两棵树。他蹲在枣树前面看了很久，然后站起来，跑到方圆面前，“方圆哥，你看到没有，那棵杏树结果了！”方圆走过去，蹲下看了看。果然，杏树的枝条上挂着几粒青色的小果子，比上次看的时候大了一圈，圆滚滚的，硬邦邦的。“真的结果了。”“那什么时候能吃？”“还要等一个多月。等它变黄了，就能吃了。”方小石看着那些小果子，又蹲下来看了一会儿才站起来。他站起来的时候，拍了拍膝盖上的泥土，又看了一圈院子，像是想把整个夏天都记住。
杏树结果的消息，很快就传到了方正阳那里。第二天下午，方正阳背着手溜达到了院门口，没有进来，只是站在门口朝院子里看了看。他的目光先是落在那棵枣树上，慢慢移到旁边的杏树上，又落到树下那棵小枣树上，来回看了一遍。“这两棵树长得不错。”方圆从屋里走出来，“刚结的果，还青着。”“青着好。青着说明还在长。”方正阳没有再多说，背着手转身走了。
傍晚的时候，方圆坐在石桌旁，把李子酱打开，又尝了一口。甜味在嘴里化开，比昨天更深了一些，像是腌了一夜的时光终于沉下去了。王紫璇从厨房出来，在他对面坐下。“甜吗？”“甜。”“那你多吃点。”方圆又吃了一勺，然后把盖子盖好，放回桌上。“紫璇。”“嗯？”“下个月方家族会，你真的要去？”“去。”“那你穿什么？”王紫璇低头看了看自己身上的旧衣服，“我到时候找一件干净的衣服。”方圆没有说话。他站起来，走进屋里，过了一会儿，拿出一件叠好的浅蓝色布衣，放在桌上。“上次在东市看到的，觉得你穿应该合适。”王紫璇愣了一下，伸手摸了摸那件衣服的料子。棉布的，洗过一水之后微微发皱，但颜色很好看，像是初夏的天空。“你什么时候买的？”“上次你说要去族会的时候。”王紫璇没有说谢谢，也没有说别的。她把衣服叠好，抱在怀里，站起来，“我去试试。”她转身走进屋里，门在她身后轻轻合上了。
月亮升起来的时候，王紫璇穿着那件浅蓝色的衣服从屋里走出来。方圆坐在石凳上，看到她站在门口，月光照在她身上。她没有走过来，只是站在门口，让他看。他看了一会儿，然后说了一句：“挺合身的。”王紫璇没有回答。她走回屋里，把衣服换下来，叠好，放在枕头旁边，像放一件要留很久的东西。她在床边坐了一会儿，手搭在那件衣服上，布料在指腹下有一点微微的凉，像是有什么话被叠进了针脚里，等着她什么时候穿上了，再慢慢说出来。
第二天，王紫璇穿着那件浅蓝色的衣服来了。她在院子里走来走去，浇花，给两棵树松土，偶尔蹲下来拔几棵野草，像是要为这件衣服找一个最自然的方式待在这个院子里。方圆没有多看她，但每次走过院子，余光里总会碰到那片浅蓝色，像天空的一角落了进来。傍晚的时候，她坐在石桌旁削一个梨，削得很慢，皮没有断。她低着头，专注地看着手里的刀尖，梨皮一圈一圈地落下来，堆在石桌上，像一封没有寄出的信。
夏天还很长，院子里的杏树还在长，枣树也在长。那件浅蓝色的衣服叠好之后又穿了几次，每次穿完都被她重新叠好，没有留下什么褶皱。方小石隔几天来一次，每次来都要蹲在杏树前面看那些青色的小果子长大了多少。方正阳偶尔路过，背着手看一眼，不说话，也不多留。方圆每天早晨起来先去井边打水洗脸，然后蹲在树前面，看一看两棵树的长势，顺手扶正一根被风吹歪的枝条。然后站起来，走进厨房，生火煮粥。粥滚了，水面冒起细密的气泡。他把火调小，盖上盖子，站在灶台前等它慢慢熬好。外面的天渐渐亮透了，光从窗口斜斜照进来，他知道王紫璇快来了。他听着锅里的声响，忽然觉得，日子不是在向前赶，而是在一圈一圈地绕回来，越绕越紧，越绕越稳。他端起那碗刚刚好的粥，转身走出厨房。
：8xiaoshuo。：wap.8xiaoshuo
content_en:
On the day the plum sauce was ready, Qingzhou City had its first heavy rain since the beginning of summer.
It started to rain in the afternoon, and the sky suddenly darkened, as if someone had covered the city with a gray cloth. The wind was so strong that it turned the leaves of the locust tree over, revealing the light white veins on the back. Fangyuan stood at the door of the main room, watching the rain fall. The raindrops hit the bluestone slab, causing white water splashes to form, which soon formed into a trickle and flowed downwards along the cracks in the stone slab. Wang Zixuan stuck her head out from the kitchen, "What are you doing standing there? Come in and take shelter from the rain." Fangyuan walked back into the house and sat down on the threshold. The sound of rain hitting the tiles was thick, like someone beating a snare drum on the roof.
"The plum jam is ready." Wang Zixuan put a small clay pot on the table, "Try it." Fangyuan stood up, walked to the table, and opened the lid. The sauce is dark red, shiny, and exudes a light sweet aroma. He dipped a little in his hand and put it in his mouth. Sweet, a little sour, with a long aftertaste. "It's delicious," he said. Wang Zixuan didn't speak. The corners of her mouth curved slightly, as if she was smiling or confirming something. She closed the lid and put it back on the table, "Let it sit and eat slowly."
The rain kept falling and showed no sign of stopping. There was water in the yard, and the well was half submerged. The two trees stood in the rain, being blown around by the wind, but their roots were firmly rooted. Fangyuan stood at the window and looked at it for a while, then walked back and sat down. "Will the trees be okay?" Wang Zixuan was also standing at the window watching, "No. They have already taken root." When she said this, her tone was very normal. Fangyuan did not answer, but just leaned on the back of the chair, listening to the sound of rain, as if she had been waiting for the rain all summer long.
In the evening, the rain became lighter. Fang Xiaoshi ran over holding an umbrella and stood at the door, water dripping from the umbrella. "Brother Fangyuan, my mother asked me to come and see you. She said that with such a heavy rain, will the two trees in your yard be washed down?" "No. The roots are deep." Fang Xiaoshi looked over and confirmed that the trees were still standing firmly, and nodded, "Then I will go back. My mother is still waiting for me to go back for dinner." He ran away with an umbrella, splashing when he stepped over the puddles.
After the rain stopped, the air in the yard became very clean, the bluestones were washed until they were shiny, and even the moss in the corners of the wall was a little green. When Fang Xiaoshi came the next day, the first thing he did was to look at the two trees. He squatted in front of the jujube tree and looked at it for a long time, then stood up and ran to Fangyuan, "Brother Fangyuan, did you see that the apricot tree has produced fruit!" Fangyuan walked over, knelt down and took a look. Sure enough, there were a few small green fruits hanging on the branches of the apricot tree, which were larger than the last time I saw them, round and hard. "The fruit has really come out." "When can we eat it?" "It will take more than a month. When it turns yellow, you can eat it." Fang Xiaoshi looked at the small fruits, squatted down and looked at them for a while before standing up. When he stood up, he patted the dirt on his knees and looked around the yard again, as if he wanted to remember the whole summer.
The news of the apricot tree's fruiting soon reached Fang Zhengyang. In the afternoon of the next day, Fang Zhengyang walked to the courtyard gate with his hands behind his back. He didn't come in. He just stood at the door and looked into the courtyard. His eyes first fell on the jujube tree, then slowly moved to the apricot tree next to it, and then to the small jujube tree under the tree, looking back and forth. "These two trees are growing well." Fang Yuan walked out of the house, "The newly borne fruits are still green." "It's good to be green. Being green means they are still growing." Fang Zhengyang said no more, turned around and left with his hands behind his back.
In the evening, Fang Yuan sat at the stone table, opened the plum jam, and took another bite. The sweetness melted in your mouth, and it was a little deeper than yesterday, as if it had been marinated all night and finally settled. Wang Zixuan came out of the kitchen and sat down opposite him. "Is it sweet?" "Sweet." "Then you eat more." Fangyuan ate againI took a spoonful, then put the lid on and put it back on the table. "Zixuan." "Huh?" "Do you really want to go to the Fang family meeting next month?" "Go." "Then what are you wearing?" Wang Zixuan looked down at the old clothes on her body, "I'll find some clean clothes then." Fang Yuan said nothing. He stood up and walked into the room. After a while, he took out a folded light blue cloth and placed it on the table. "I saw it in Dongshi last time. I think it should suit you well." Wang Zixuan was stunned for a moment and reached out to touch the material of the dress. It's cotton, slightly wrinkled after being washed, but the color is beautiful, like the sky in early summer. "When did you buy it?" "Last time you said you were going to the clan meeting." Wang Zixuan didn't say thank you or anything else. She folded the clothes, held them in her arms, and stood up, "I'll try it." She turned around and walked into the house, and the door closed gently behind her.
When the moon rose, Wang Zixuan walked out of the house wearing that light blue dress. Fangyuan was sitting on the stone bench and saw her standing at the door, the moonlight shining on her. She didn't come over, just stood at the door and let him look. He looked at it for a while, and then said: "It fits well." Wang Zixuan did not answer. She walked back into the house, changed out of her clothes, folded them, and placed them next to the pillow, like putting something she would keep for a long time. She sat by the bed for a while, putting her hands on the dress. The fabric was slightly cool under her fingertips, as if something had been folded into the stitches, waiting for her to put it on, and then say it out slowly.
The next day, Wang Zixuan came wearing that light blue dress. She walked around the yard, watered the flowers, loosened the soil on two trees, and occasionally squatted down to pull out a few weeds, as if she was trying to find the most natural way for this piece of clothing to stay in the yard. Fangyuan didn't look at her much, but every time she walked through the yard, she would always see the light blue in her peripheral vision, like a corner of the sky coming in. In the evening, she sat at the stone table and peeled a pear, peeling it very slowly without breaking the skin. She lowered her head and looked at the tip of the knife in her hand intently. The pear skin fell down in circles and piled on the stone table, like an unsent letter.
Summer is still very long, the apricot trees and jujube trees in the yard are still growing. The light blue dress was folded and worn several times. She folded it again after each wear, leaving no wrinkles. Fang Xiaoshi comes here every few days, and every time he comes, he squats in front of the apricot tree to see how much the small green fruits have grown. Fang Zhengyang occasionally passed by and took a look with his hands behind his back, but said nothing and didn't stay much. When Fangyuan gets up every morning, he first goes to the well to fetch water and wash his face. Then he squats in front of the tree, looks at the growth of the two trees, and straightens a branch that has been blown by the wind. Then he stood up, walked into the kitchen, lit a fire and cooked porridge. The porridge is boiling, and fine bubbles appear on the water. He turned down the heat, closed the lid, and stood in front of the stove, waiting for it to simmer slowly. The sky outside was getting brighter, and the light shone in from the window. He knew that Wang Zixuan was coming soon. Listening to the sound in the pot, he suddenly felt that the days were not rushing forward, but coming back in circles, getting tighter and more stable. He picked up the bowl of porridge, turned around and walked out of the kitchen.
